findings.issue: The new test covers withOpponentStyles itself, but nothing checks that onChange actually calls it. renderToString cannot fire events, so if onChange skipped the helper and spread `settings ?? DEFAULT_SETTINGS` inline, every test would still pass. The risk is small: the App-shaped `disabled=""` assertion is now tested, and a disabled input fires no change events, so the guard is a second layer of protection.
findings.evidence: SettingsScreen.tsx:50-53 onChange -> withOpponentStyles(settings, e.currentTarget.checked); tests/ui/opponent-styles.acceptance.test.tsx only calls withOpponentStyles directly.
findings.fix: Optional: leave as is. Or, if a DOM test harness is added later, fire a change event on the loading render and assert onSettingsChange was not called.

summary: The round-1 MAJOR tests/ui/opponent-styles.acceptance.test.tsx:disabled-until-loaded-guard-untested is resolved. I re-ran both mutations on SettingsScreen.tsx and restored the file each time. (1) Changing `disabled` to `onSettingsChange === undefined` makes the SPEC-01 test fail on the App-shaped loading render. (2) Replacing the guard with `{ ...(settings ?? DEFAULT_SETTINGS), showOpponentStyles }` makes the withOpponentStyles unit test fail. The test-file diff since r1 only adds lines; no assertion was removed or loosened. The locked hash and snapshot were re-recorded (23 to 28 assertions). Regression check: withOpponentStyles is a small pure function and its doc comment says what it does. The onChange handler keeps the same behaviour: nothing is sent while loading, and once loaded the whole record is sent. There is no scope creep. The only remaining gap is that the onChange-to-helper wiring is not tested (MINOR).
